general_information.Description: The course focuses on process intelligence gathering and intelligence analysis with target-centric approach method. Describe some ways to increase the effectiveness of the of predict analysis. The course provides a general guide to help students understand the technical intelligence analysis. Assessment scheme: 1. On-going assessment: + Quiz: 4 quizzes, 20% (5% per each) + Project review: 10% + Assignment: 30% + Presentation: 10% 2. Final exam: 30% 3. Total: 100% Evaluation criteria: Completion Criteria: Every on-going assessment component > 0, Final Result >=5 & Final Exam Score >=4
general_information.Tools: 1. Jigsaw: http://www.cc.gatech.edu/gvu/ii/jigsaw/ 2. NodeXL: nodexl.codeplex.com 3. Microsoft Excel 2013

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Introducing the subject, mode of teaching and learning, course evaluation criterias. Introduction to the nature of Intelligence.

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Explain the process of intelligence. Introduce to the traditional intelligence cycle and the target-centric process. Classification of targets: complex systems and networks.

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Defining the intelligence problems (customers, product, target, …)

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Explain the approach method Strategies- to-Task and counterintelligence problem.

schedule.Topic: An Analysis Approach to the Target
schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Explain the analysis approach to the target. Explain the concept of a model and the method using target models for analysis.

schedule.Topic: An Analysis Approach to the Target
schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Introduce to the counterintelligence analysis model and the target model combinations.

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Presentation of the analytic spectrum, shows the results of the analysis. The indications and warnings may result from information analysis.

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Quiz 1 Explain the methods to create a conceptual model. Introduce the generic models: Lists, Curves, Comparative Modeling, Pattern Models, Relationship Models, Profiles, Process Models, Simulation Models.

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Introduce the combination models: Geospatial Models, Human Terrain Models, Space-Time Models. Introduce the Geographic Profiling, a kind of the Geospatial Model.

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Classification the sources of intellignece information. Literal sources: Open Source, Human Intelligence, Communications Intelligence, Cyber Collection.

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Nonliteral sources: Remote and In Situ Sensing, Imaging and Spectral Sensing, Passive Radiofrequency Intelligence, Radar Intelligence, Geophysical and Nuclear Intelligence, Materiel and Materials Collection, Biometrics.

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Explain the evaluating and collating data. Evaluating evidence using evaluating the source and evaluating the communications channel through which the information arrived.

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Evaluating by using combining evidence, collating between them, considering the degree of convergent and divergent. Project (deployment - guide)

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Introduce the collection strategies. Four steps to develop the collection strategies: 1. The Problem Breakdown and Target Model Relationship 2. Identifying Gaps

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: 3. Developing the Collection Strategy 4. Planning for Future Collection

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Denial and deception (called D&D) are major weapons in the counterintelligence arsenal of a country or organization.

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Signaling is the opposite of D&D. It is the process of deliberately sending a message, usually to an opposing intelligence service. Recognizing and interpreting an opponent’s signals is one of the more difficult challenges an analyst must face.

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Quiz 2 Presented a large number of analytical methodologies are available to the analyst. Some of the most useful fall into the two broad categories of structured argumentation and alternative or competitive analysis.

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: A third category of analytical methodologies, predictive methodologies, is disscused here.The highest form of intelligence analysis requires structured thinking that results in a prediction of what is likely to happen.

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Introduce the preditive approach. Intelligence scenarios, the result of preditive, are descriptions in story form of a future target model.

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Analysis involves predicting the future state of a target by using one of three means—extrapolation (unchanging forces), projection (changing forces), and forecasting (changing and new forces).

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Predictive analysis relies on assessing the impact of forces that shape organizations, lead to new developments, and motivate people. Explain the forces: inertia, countervailing forces, contamination.

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Explain the forces: synergy, feedback, regulation. Review Project

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Quiz 3 To analyze an organization, one must examine its structure, function, and process. Structure analysis focus on relationship of most interest to the intelligence customer. Functional analysis focus on behavior, specifically on the decision-making process. Process analysis focus the flows and vulnerable points within system.

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Technology analysis is used in business intelligence, where it can provide companies with a competitive advantage, and in military intelligence, where it is of value in assessing the performance of current and future weapons systems. It can be used to assess the future performance of a technology, the use or transfer of the technology, or in forecasts of technology breakthroughs. Most simulation models are systems of equations that must be solved for different input assumptions.

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Focus on the customers and purposes of analysis. It describes the intelligence requirements of various clients in government and the private sector, and the purposes/objectives that intelligence has in serving those clients. Classification the different customers (policymakers, congress, business leaders, …). Explain the preparing and presenting analysis results.

schedule.Student Materials: Robert M. Clark - Intelligence analysis : a target-centric approach, Fourth Edition - CQ Press, 2013. ISBN 978-1-4522-0612-7
schedule.Student's Tasks: Focus on two types of management. The principles also apply to analysts who must manage the target-centric process. The increasing collaboration among analysts, customers, and collectors requires that someone manage the effort. Focus on the structure and function of the analytic unit. Then we take up the management of the process including tradecraft and analytic methodologies.
Quiz 4 Presented in groups (3-4 students). Topics in the part "After class activities". Evaluating the results of students applying knowledge from the course.
